battle.name: 張金稱起義
battle.brief: 大業七年冬，河北易縣的張金稱聚眾起事，以符水聚民，旬月之間眾至數萬，與高士達等部互為聲援，擁兵十餘萬。隋廷遣將討伐，他最遲在大業十二年死於與高士達的爭鬥，部眾多歸竇建德。卡面的希臘重步兵並不在河北，但它是一面鏡子：以裝備維繫的方陣，與以飢寒維繫的鄉兵，中間隔著隋朝崩塌的距離。

kit.name: 希臘重步兵
kit.history: 方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽。盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實。

countries: 交戰的兩方是隋朝官軍與河北一帶的起義集團。隋朝方面，兵源分三路：一是府兵舊制崩壞之後仍被朝廷點集的州縣鄉兵，二是禁軍與臨時招募的募兵，三是北方邊郡與行台麾下的契丹、靺鞨、突厥降附騎兵。指揮系統上，隋廷以郡為基本單位，郡丞與縣令自募自練，各州置總管府，出兵則由行軍總管率領；大業年間河北用兵的重心放在涿郡一線，涿郡既是北方邊鎮，也是長城沿線的轉輸樞紐，官軍糧秣由太原、范陽方向運來，兵源則靠各州臨時抽調。起義方並非一支統一軍隊，而是河北、平北數個互不隸屬的武裝集團，張金稱、高士達、孫安祖各自樹旗聚眾，彼此以馳援和響應相接，並沒有誰向誰歸屬。集團內部是首領、部曲、村社三層結構：首領以符水一類的民間方術取得信眾的服從，部曲多為同鄉同里，鄉里則供應糧秣、嚮導、渡口與消息。河北自東晉末以來一直是中原馬政與北方邊軍的交會之地，義軍手中雖無正規甲兵，卻有能迅速上馬的散馬與本地兵匠，因此起義集團的機動性遠高於一般郡兵。兩軍在河北平原上對峙，表面是起義者與官軍之爭，實際是三征高句麗抽空河北之後，地方軍事秩序斷裂所留下的一段真空。
countriesEn: The two sides were the Sui government's armies and the insurgent bands of the Hebei region. On the Sui side the manpower came from three channels: the county levies still mustered by the court after the old fubing system had broken down, the imperial guards together with troops hired on the spot, and the Xianbei, Mohe and Turkic horsemen attached to the northern commanderies and to the regional military governors. The command structure ran on a county basis: commandery lieutenants and county magistrates raised and trained their own men, each prefecture carried a chief military office, and field armies were led by mobile commanders. During the Daye years the weight of the Hebei war sat on the Zhuojun line, for Zhuojun was both a northern frontier town and a transshipment hub along the Great Wall, and the grain and supplies of the imperial armies came from the Taiyuan and Fanyang directions while the soldiers were scraped together from every prefecture. The insurgents were not a single army at all but a number of mutually independent armed groups across Hebei and northern Ping; Zhang Jincheng, Gao Shida and Sun Anzu each raised their own banner and gathered their own men, and they supported one another by reinforcement and by answering each other's calls, with none of them subordinate to any of the others. Each group had three layers: the leader, the bands of dependents, and the village community. The leader obtained obedience through folk magic of the water-blessing kind, the bands were mostly neighbours and kinsmen from the same villages, and the villages supplied grain, guides, fords and news. Since the end of the Eastern Jin, Hebei had been the meeting place of the Central Plain horse system and the northern frontier garrisons, so although the insurgents had no regular armour they did have loose horses that could be mounted quickly and the smiths of the countryside; their mobility was therefore far above that of an ordinary county militia. The confrontation on the Hebei plain looked like a rising against the government, but in truth it filled the vacuum left by a shattered local military order once the three campaigns against Goguryeo had drawn away the strength of Hebei.
people: 史書留下的名字不多，能夠確定的是以下幾位。張金稱是起義的直接首領，河北易縣一帶人，起兵之初人數甚少，靠符水與符籙一類的民間方術聚眾，旬月之間由數百增至數萬，後與高士達部合流，眾至十餘萬，一度壓過河北各縣。他不是受過專門軍事訓練的統帥，起義初期並未建立嚴整的編制，這一點在他後來與高士達的相爭中暴露無遺。高士達是高句麗人，同樣在河北起兵，兵力號稱十餘萬，與張金稱時而並肩、時而相疑；兩家曾合兵攻打涿郡，攻城不下而內部爭雄，張金稱死在這場合作破裂的餘波裡，舊史對具體經過只有寥寥數語，或說為高士達所謀，或說死於本部眾的爭鬥。竇建德是河北涿郡一帶的鄉里豪右，早年在隋將張須陀麾下效力，張須陀陣亡之後才聚眾自起；張金稱與高士達兩部的散卒、以及河北的亂民，大量流入他的麾下，使他很快成為河北最有力的武裝首領，後來建邦號為夏，定都樂壽，與瓦崗的李密爭奪河北與山東。隋朝方面的關鍵人物是張須陀，他以驍勇善戰聞名，屢次率騎兵搜索追擊河北的起義軍，斬獲以萬計，是隋廷鎮壓河北的主要支柱；後來他奉調進京，中途病死在押解途中，河北戰局隨即失去唯一能獨當一面的重兵統帥。背景人物是隋煬帝楊廣：大業年間三次征高句麗、巡遊江都、廣修運河與宮室，加倍的徭役兵役正是河北民變的直接推手。同期起義的王薄在山東長平最早響應，孫安祖則在渤海一帶聚眾，河北與山東的起義由此連成一條線。
peopleEn: The histories preserve only a handful of names, and the following are the ones that can be established. Zhang Jincheng was the immediate leader of the rising, a man of the Yixian area of Hebei. He began with very few followers and gathered them by means of blessed water and written talismans, the most of the sort of folk magic, growing from a few hundred to several tens of thousands within a month; he then joined forces with Gao Shida's band, the combined force being credited with more than a hundred thousand men, and for a time overawing the counties of Hebei. He was not a commander trained in war: the rising began without any regular organisation, and that showed plainly afterwards in his quarrel with Gao Shida. Gao Shida was a Goguryeo man who had risen in Hebei as well, with a force likewise reckoned at more than a hundred thousand; he stood shoulder to shoulder with Zhang Jincheng at one moment and distrusted him at the next. The two once marched together against Zhuojun, failed to take it, and fell to quarrelling over who should lead; Zhang Jincheng died in the aftermath of that broken alliance. The old records give only a few words for the manner of it, saying variously that he was plotted against by Gao Shida or that he was killed in a strife within his own ranks. Dou Jiande was a local notable of the Zhuojun district who had served under the Sui general Zhang Xutuo and only gathered a following of his own after that general's death; the stragglers of Zhang Jincheng's and Gao Shida's bands, together with the displaced people of Hebei, poured into his command in large numbers, and he soon became the strongest armed leader in the region, later founding the state of Xia with its capital at Leshou and contesting Hebei and western Shandong with Li Mi at Wagang. The key Sui figure was Zhang Xutuo, famous for dash and for repeated mounted pursuit of the Hebei insurgents, with kills and captures counted by the tens of thousands; he was the main prop of the court's suppression effort in Hebei. Later, when he was summoned to the capital, he fell ill and died on the road under escort, and the Hebei war lost at once the only heavy commander able to hold the line by himself. Behind it all stands Sui Yangdi, Emperor Wen: the three campaigns against Goguryeo, the tours of Jiangdu, the new canal and the new palaces, and the doubling of corvée and conscription were the direct push behind the Hebei rising. Wang Bo, rising first at Changping in eastern Shandong, and Sun Anzu, gathering men around the Bohai region, linked the uprisings of Hebei and Shandong into a single line.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是希臘重步兵，即西元前五世紀以後盛行於希臘城邦的hoplite：一人一盾，圓形大盾蒙皮包邊，兩米有餘的長矛，青銅頭盔、青銅或亞麻胸甲、胫甲，一整套裝備由本人自備，所以被稱為重步兵。它的打法是密集方陣，盾牌左右相疊、彼此遮蔽，矛尖越過前排肩頭指向前方，陣伍依號令前進，頂住衝鋒之後再以短兵相接的近戰決勝負。放到六一一年河北的戰場上，這件兵器只能當作一面對照的鏡子，而不是在場的裝備。起義者的武器極為簡陋：削尖的竹木桿、綁上刃口的木柄刀、耒耜改造的短兵、獵弓與箭矢，鎧甲極少，多是從陣亡官軍手中繳獲的零散甲片，皮甲與布甲也只見於少數骨幹。隋朝官軍的裝備則自成體系：明光甲與札甲、長槊、腰弩與擘張弩、刀劍，攻城另有雲梯、擲石砲車與水攻之具，騎兵數量可觀，因為河北正是北方邊軍與馬市交會的地帶，義軍與官軍都在那裡搶奪馬匹。若要找與希臘方陣真正相通的東西，反而在隋朝自己的兵書裡：《李衛公問對》所載用兵之法中有以大陣包小陣、旗號別而進的編組思路，步兵居中結陣、騎兵分張兩翼，同樣是把正面密度當成戰役勝算的買賣，只是隋軍的方陣天生要應付北方草原的騎兵，而希臘方陣正是為了擋住馬的衝鋒而生。制度上的對比更尖銳：希臘城邦以土地與公民權保障重步兵自備全套裝備，河北鄉民則在饑寒與徭役之下把農具變成兵器，同樣是田間人口組成的隊伍，一邊有保障，一邊只剩下絕望。
kitsEn: The piece on the card is the Greek hoplite, the heavy infantryman of the fifth century BC and after in the Greek city-states: a man with a shield, a large round shield of covered and edged timber, a spear more than two metres long, a bronze helmet, a bronze or linen cuirass and greaves, with the whole outfit supplied by the man himself, which is why he was called a heavy soldier. His way of fighting was the dense phalanx: shields overlapped sideways so that each covered the next, spear points projected over the shoulders of the front rank, the file advanced on the word of command, absorbed the charge, and then settled the matter in close combat with edged weapons. Set that against a Hebei battlefield in 611 CE, the piece can only serve as a mirror for comparison, not as equipment present on the ground. The arms of the insurgents were extremely simple: sharpened bamboo and wooden poles, wooden-hafted blades with edges lashed on, short weapons cut from mattocks, hunting bows and arrows. Armour was scarce, mostly a few scattered plates taken from government soldiers who had fallen, and leather or cloth armour appears only on a handful of the core men. The Sui armies had a system of their own: mingguang and zhajia armour, long spears, crossbows of the waist-mounted and shoulder-drawn types, sabres and swords, and for siege work scaling ladders, stone-throwing trebuchots and the use of water. Their cavalry was numerous, since Hebei was where the northern frontier garrisons and the horse markets met, and both the insurgents and the government fought for the animals. If one looks for something genuinely continuous with the Greek phalanx, it is not in Hebei but in the Sui military books themselves: the methods of war recorded in the Questions and Answers between Tang Taizong and Li Weigong include an organisation of great array enclosing small array, with separate banners advancing separately, infantry forming the centre and cavalry posted on the wings, again treating the density of the front as the currency of a battle. The difference is that the Sui array was born to meet horse from the northern steppe, while the Greek phalanx was born to stop a horse charge in the first place. The contrast in institutions is sharper still: the Greek city-state guaranteed the hoplite's full equipment through land and citizenship, while the peasants of Hebei, under hunger and corvée, turned their farm tools into weapons. Both were armies drawn from the countryside, but one had guarantees behind it and the other had nothing left but despair.
tactics: 起義的戰法大半只能從結果反推。張金稱部起兵並非出自任何兵書，而是以符水建立信眾網絡，靠人與人之間的傳播在鄉里之間迅速蔓延，作戰則沿用河北民間原有的自衛方式：憑村社結寨、依山澤與河渠藏身、夜間襲擾城邑與糧倉、得糧即散、官軍一到便退回鄉里。河北平原地勢開闊，官軍精騎在視野與機動上佔優，義軍若要在野戰中取勝，只能靠人數與多點同時爆發的混亂，因此他們多選在郡縣守備空虛、糧倉有存、驛傳不繼的時機發動，一度攻陷不少州縣，又迅速轉入流動，把官軍拖成一處一處的分兵。張金稱與高士達合兵攻涿郡，是起義軍第一次把兩個集團捏在一起作大手筆，卻也暴露了聯軍最脆弱處：兩家沒有可以服眾的統一指揮，攻城器械、糧秣分配與進攻次序都談不攏，圍城既久則內部互疑，張金稱最終死在這次合作破裂之後。隋軍的戰法則是另一路：以張須陀為首，用精騎搜索、追擊與截斷義軍的散兵，步卒結陣以弩手前壓、槊兵居中，攻城靠砲車與雲梯，必要時以水壅灌城，糧道則倚太原、范陽轉輸維繫。義軍與官軍的反覆較量，實際是流動作戰與騎兵追擊之間的較量；最後是義軍內部的分裂先一步發生，才讓官軍得以各个擊破，而張金稱本人至死沒有取得一次正面會戰的勝利。
tacticsEn: The tactics of the rising can largely be reconstructed backwards from its results. Zhang Jincheng's movement did not draw on any manual of war: it was built on a network of believers created by blessed water, spreading from person to person through the villages, and in the field it used the self-defence customs already known in Hebei countryside society: rallying at the village, hiding among the hills, marshes and watercourses, raiding towns and granaries by night, breaking off with the grain once taken, and withdrawing into the villages whenever government troops arrived. On the open plain of Hebei the government cavalry held the advantage in sight-lines and manoeuvre, so the insurgents could only hope to win in the open through numbers and through the confusion of simultaneous outbreaks at many points. They therefore chose the moments when county garrisons were thin, granaries were full and the courier network was broken, seized a number of prefectures, and then went mobile again, forcing the government to chase them in scattered columns. The joint siege of Zhuojun by Zhang Jincheng and Gao Shida was the first time the insurgents fused two groups into a great operation, and it exposed the weakest point of any such alliance: the two houses had no single command they would both obey, they could not agree on siege equipment, the distribution of grain or the order of assault, and once the siege dragged on each began to suspect the other. Zhang Jincheng died in the ruins of that collaboration. The Sui method ran in the opposite direction: under Zhang Xutuo, cavalry searched, pursued and cut off the scattered bands, infantry formed up with crossbowmen pressing from the front and spearmen in the centre, siege work was done with trebuchots and ladders and, where needed, water released against the walls, while the supply line hung on the transport from Taiyuan and Fanyang. The repeated clash between the two sides was in truth a contest between mobile raiding and mounted pursuit, and in the end it was the split inside the insurgent camp that came first, which allowed the government to defeat the parts one at a time. Zhang Jincheng himself never won a single set-piece engagement.
data: 可核實的數字並不多，以下幾項大致可靠。時間軸是：大業七年（611）冬起兵，至大業十二年（616）張金稱死，前後約五個年頭；同期河北與山東還有高士達、孫安祖、王薄等部，其中王薄在山東長平最早響應。兵眾規模方面，舊史多作「眾至十餘萬」的概略說法，張金稱與高士達兩部各被記為十餘萬人，數目顯然是概數，但可以確定河北起義的人數已達到足以威脅郡縣、能夠攻陷州縣的程度。隋廷的壓力也可從另一組數字看出：大業八年第一次征高句麗，詔天下諸軍百餘萬人出擊，後兩次又各發數十萬，兵役與轉運同時壓在河北壯丁身上；同一時期隋煬帝北巡抵達涿郡，舊書記他在邊鎮逗留半年以上乃至十六個月不返，河北的兵備因此更加空虛。距離上，易縣與涿郡相距不足兩百里，義軍在河北境內的調動多在數日之內完成，張金稱與高士達合兵圍涿郡的路程不遠；官軍討伐的戰果，張須陀的傳記屢稱斬獲以萬計、俘虜數萬。關於死傷，舊史只留下「張金稱死」「眾潰散」「部眾歸竇建德」一類的結果性記載，具體數字已無從核對，因此只能說河北起義在五年間消耗了隋朝大量兵員與糧秣，而張金稱本人死於己方的爭鬥而非戰陣之傷，這一點可以確定。
dataEn: Verifiable numbers are scarce, and the following are the ones that can be relied on. The time axis runs from the winter of Daye 7 (611), when the rising began, to Daye 12 (616), when Zhang Jincheng died, a span of roughly five years; in the same period there were bands under Gao Shida, Sun Anzu and Wang Bo in Hebei and Shandong, Wang Bo at Changping in eastern Shandong being the earliest to answer. As for the size of the forces, the old histories give the general formula that they numbered more than a hundred thousand, both Zhang Jincheng's and Gao Shida's being reckoned at that figure; the numbers are plainly round, but it can be established that the rising in Hebei reached a scale sufficient to overawe the counties and to take prefectures. The pressure from the Sui side can be read from another set of figures: for the first campaign against Goguryeo in Daye 8 the edict mustered more than a million men from all the armies of the realm, and the two campaigns that followed each raised several hundred thousand more, so that conscription and transport fell at once on the able-bodied men of Hebei; in the same period Yangdi toured north to Zhuojun, where the old books have him lingering at the frontier town for more than half a year, even sixteen months by the usual reckoning, without returning, so that the garrisoning of Hebei grew thinner still. As for distance, Yixian and Zhuojun lie less than two hundred li apart, so the movements of the insurgents inside Hebei were accomplished in a matter of days, and the road from the joint siege of Zhuojun was short. On the other side, the results of the government campaigns are repeatedly described in the biography of Zhang Xutuo as kills and prisoners counted by the tens of thousands. As for casualties, the old histories preserve only result-of-battle statements such as that Zhang Jincheng died, that the host broke up, and that his men went over to Dou Jiande; the precise figures cannot be checked any longer. What can be said is that the Hebei rising consumed a great many soldiers and a great deal of grain and transport on the Sui side over those five years, and that Zhang Jincheng himself died in a strife of his own camp rather than in a pitched battle.
cause: 起義的直接原因可以分成遠近兩層。近的一層是當地社會的崩解：大業年間連年水旱，冀州一帶多次饑荒，朝廷雖下詔免租賑恤，真正到達鄉里的數目有限；官吏苛暴，州郡豪強兼併土地與戶口，租調之外還有各種雜斂，鄉民一旦歉收便無以為生。遠的一層是國家把河北的壯丁與錢糧抽去打仗。大業八年起三次征高句麗，每次發兵以十萬計，轉輸的役夫、車馬沿河北與山東一路北運，遼東戰事失利之後兵役並未停止，反而加徵；修河、造舟、營宮室與守長城的徭役也壓在同一批鄉民身上，冬天徵役尤其嚴酷。起義的時機正是防守的空隙：河北的壯丁與錢糧被抽往遼東，郡縣只剩老弱與臨時募來的鄉兵，官府催督租稅又更急，於是民間流傳著對三征高句麗的怨恨，期待有人先動手。外部環境同樣重要：北方契丹、突厥在邊地往來頻繁，涿郡一帶既要防外又要平叛，官軍調度始終捉襟見肘，點集的兵員多半是臨時湊數。第一次征高句麗的敗績傳回河北的時間，恰好與起義的爆發重疊，於是起義的號召不再需要太多說服。
causeEn: The immediate causes of the rising can be divided into a near and a far layer. The near layer was the breakdown of local society: through the Daye years there were repeated floods and droughts and more than one famine in the Jizhou region; the court issued edicts remitting taxes and sending relief, but very little of that reached the villages. Magistrates were harsh, powerful local families swallowed land and households, and besides the regular levies and taxes there were all kinds of exactions, so that a single failed harvest left the peasants with nothing. The far layer was that the state was drawing the able-bodied men and the money and grain of Hebei away to fight. From Daye 8 the three campaigns against Goguryeo each mustered hundreds of thousands, and the corvée porters, wagons and draught animals were dragged along the roads of Hebei and Shandong towards Liaodong; when the campaign in Liaodong failed, the conscription did not stop but was increased. Building the canal, the great ships, the new palaces and the northern wall all fell on the same peasants, and winter levies were particularly harsh. The moment of the rising was also a gap in the defences: the men and the stores of Hebei had been drawn away to Liaodong, the counties were left with the old and the weak and with hastily enrolled militia, and the officials pressed harder than ever for the taxes, so that resentment over the Goguryeo campaigns ran through the countryside and people waited for someone to move first. The external environment mattered as well: Khitan and Turkic groups were moving along the northern frontier all the time, and the Zhuojun line had to watch outward against them and inward against the rebels at once, so the government could never gather its forces in one place, and most of the troops it did assemble were mustered on the spot. The news of the defeat in the first Goguryeo campaign reached Hebei at very nearly the moment the rising broke out, and from then on the call to arms needed very little persuasion.
impact: 張金稱起義的直接後果，是河北在往後十年裡再沒有恢復安寧。義軍的出現證明了隋廷的徵兵體系已經無法把河北的社會重新壓住：郡縣被攻陷、糧倉被掠走、驛傳斷絕，州郡的守官有的據城自保，有的棄城而逃。張金稱死後，他留下來的河北武裝並沒有消失，而是被竇建德整編接管，竇建德以河北為根據地，與瓦崗的李密爭奪河北與山東，最後建國為夏，一度是唐初北方最大的割據力量之一。這條線的終點在武德四年（621）的虎牢關：唐軍擊破竇建德於虎牢，竇建德被擒於洺水，河北納入唐的版圖；而在此之前，劉黑悶又曾一度在河北重建義軍，仍是這場起義留下的群眾與部曲在起作用。制度上的影響更長久，隋朝為鎮壓河北義軍而把兵權進一步收攏到州與行軍總管，使地方與中央的武力對比改變；唐代河北尚武、層層設置節度使，最後形成河朔三鎮的割據局面，其兵風與部族結構，都可以在隋末這一代河北的戰亂中找到源頭。這場起義還給隋朝上了一課：它把以關隴舊制控天下的辦法徹底暴露在廢弛面前，隋亡之後唐承隋制而不得不大量改用募兵，河北的經驗是其中最沉重的一課；同時它也證明，只要鄉民手中的農具還能變成兵器，任何一次大規模的兵役與轉運都可能成為導火線。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of Zhang Jincheng's rising was that Hebei never recovered its peace in the decade that followed. The insurgents proved that the Sui recruiting system could no longer press Hebei's society back down: prefectures were taken, granaries emptied, the courier network broken, and the local officials either shut themselves in their walled towns or abandoned them and fled. After Zhang Jincheng died the armed force he had gathered in Hebei did not vanish; it was taken over and reorganised by Dou Jiande, who made Hebei his base and fought Li Mi of Wagang for Hebei and western Shandong before founding the state of Xia and briefly becoming the largest regional power in the north of the early Tang. The end of that line came in 621 at Hulao Pass: Tang forces broke Dou Jiande, Dou Jiande was taken at Mingshui, and Hebei passed into the Tang empire; before that, Liu Hei had already rebuilt an insurgent state in Hebei, still working with the same people and the same bands that this rising had produced. The institutional effect lasted longer. To put down the Hebei insurgents the Sui drew military authority further into the prefectures and the field commanderies, changing the balance of force between centre and locality; and the martial temper of Hebei, the layered command of military governors and the eventual regional states of the three Heshuo circuits all trace back, in their fighting style and in their tribal structure, to the wars in Hebei in the last years of the Sui. The rising also taught the Sui a lesson: it exposed the breakdown of the arrangement by which the old Guanlong military system held the empire together, so that after the Sui fell the Tang kept its institutions but had to rely far more heavily on hired soldiers, and the experience of Hebei was the heaviest part of that reckoning. The rising also demonstrated that as long as a peasant's farm tool could be turned into a weapon, any great levy and any long transport of supplies might become a fuse.
result: 張金稱這場起義的結局，是一場起於鄉里、終於內部的失敗。起兵五年之後，河北的局面已經完全改觀：張金稱本人死於大業十二年前後與高士達的爭鬥，舊史沒有留下更細的經過，但可以確定他的死不是全軍在戰陣上覆沒所致；他的部眾一部分散歸鄉里，一部分被竇建德收編，河北的起義武裝於是由張金稱時代進入竇建德時代。隋廷在短期內並沒有真正解決河北問題，張須陀這位能打的統帥在押解途中病亡，繼任者無法同時應付高士達、孫安祖與竇建德，河北的郡縣仍然是攻守不定的狀態。可以確定的結果有兩點：一是隋朝在這場消耗戰裡再沒有餘力恢復對河北的有效控制，國力反而加速下滑，兩次征高句麗的敗績與河北的戰亂互相拖累；二是河北從此成為反隋武裝的溫床，後來的竇建德、劉黑悶都從這片土壤裡產出，並在武德四年才被唐軍連根拔起。張金稱沒有留下政權，也沒有留下可延續的建制，他留下的是一個已經不肯回到編戶齊民位置的河北。對隋朝而言，真正的敗因不是某一支義軍打贏了，而是河北整個社會再也不能被國家重新編排；對後人而言，這場起義留下的最重要的記號，恰恰是卡面上那面盾牌的意義：盾牌的價值從來不在它自己，而在於左右的人能不能站到同一條線上。
resultEn: The outcome of Zhang Jincheng's rising was a failure that began in the villages and ended in internal strife. Five years after the rising started the situation in Hebei had changed completely. Zhang Jincheng himself died around Daye 12 (616) in his quarrel with Gao Shida; the old books give no finer account of it, but it is certain that his death was not the result of his whole army being wiped out on the field. Part of his men dispersed back into the villages and part were taken over by Dou Jiande, and the armed movement in Hebei thus passed from the age of Zhang Jincheng into the age of Dou Jiande. In the short term the Sui did not really settle the question of Hebei: Zhang Xutuo, the one commander who could actually fight, died of illness on the road under escort, and his successors could not deal at once with Gao Shida, Sun Anzu and Dou Jiande, so the counties of Hebei remained in a state of uncertain tenure. Two results can be established. First, in this war of attrition the Sui no longer had the strength to restore effective control over Hebei; its resources drained away faster, and the defeats in Goguryeo and the disturbances in Hebei dragged on each other. Second, Hebei became a breeding ground for armed opposition to the Sui, out of which both Dou Jiande and Liu Hei came, and it took Tang armies in 621 to root the whole thing out. Zhang Jincheng left behind no state and no institution that could be carried forward; what he left was a Hebei that would no longer consent to be counted and taxed as a register of households. For the Sui the real cause of defeat was not that some rebel army had won a battle, but that Hebei's society could no longer be re-ordered by the state; and for later readers the most telling sign left by this rising is precisely the meaning of the shield on the card. A shield was never worth anything in itself; it was worth exactly as much as the men who could stand on the same line beside it.
